parole.significato: added to nouns (people or animals) to form an adjective
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *-ьskъ, from Proto-Indo-European *-iskos.
From Proto-Slavic *a, from Proto-Indo-European *ō̃t, which is ablative form of Proto-Indo-European *e- 'this'. Cognates with Serbo-Croatian a, Russian а (a) and Czech a.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bojati, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyh₂-. First attested in the 16th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bělъ, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰēlHs (“white surface or stain”). First attested in the 16th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *byti, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH-. First attested in the 10th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bobrъ, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰébʰrus. First attested in the 16th century.

parole.significato: brother (son of the same parents as another person)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bratrъ, *bratъ, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰréh₂tēr. First attested in the 15th century.

parole.significato: to read (look at and interpret letters or other information)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bьrati (“to pick up, to take”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰéreti. For the meaning development compare with Latin lego (“to choose, to select, to collect, to gather, to read”), also compare with Russian разобра́ть (razobrátʹ, “to dismantle, to disassemble, to take apart, to decons
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *bez, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeǵʰs. First attested in the 15th century.

From da with the same meaning, from Proto-Slavic *da, from Proto-Indo-European *doh₂, which is pronoun Proto-Indo-European *de-, Proto-Indo-European *do- 'this' in lative case. Simplification occurred due to modern vowel reduction as the final /a/ reduced to /ə/.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *darъ, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₃rom. First attested in the 15th century.
From Proto-Slavic *devętь, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁néwn̥.
From Proto-Slavic *dъždžь, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dus-dyu- (“bad sky”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *dьlgъ, from Proto-Indo-European *dl̥h₁gʰós.

parole.significato: home (house or structure in which someone lives)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *domъ, from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm, from root Proto-Indo-European *dem- (“to build”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *dervo, from Proto-Indo-European *dóru.
From Proto-Slavic *(j)edinъ, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one, single”).
Contraction of earlier éden, from Proto-Slavic *(j)edinъ, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *óynos (“one, single”).
From Proto-Slavic *golъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gelH- (“naked, bald”).
From Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerH-.
From Proto-Slavic *gostь, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis.
From gostil + -na, the first being the l-participle of gostīti, itself derived from gȍst, which is from Proto-Slavic *gostь, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰóstis.
From Proto-Slavic *kъ 'to', which is itself probably from Proto-Indo-European *kwu 'where'. This form is a spirantization of k, which appeared to ease the pronunciation.
From Proto-Slavic *xoldьnъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“cold”). Compare hlád.

Derived from Proto-Slavic *i (“and”), itself from Proto-Indo-European *éy, an early locative singular determiner, formed from the root *h₁e-, *h₁o-. Cognates with Serbo-Croatian i, Macedonian и (i), Bulgarian и (i), Old Church Slavonic и (i), Czech i, Polish i, Kashubian ë, Slovak i, Belarusian і (i
From Proto-Slavic *jьgo, from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm.

A suppletive paradigm of three verbs: * The infinitive and supine from Proto-Slavic *jьti, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éyti. This verb was itself suppletive in Proto-Slavic, with a different stem for the l-participle. * The future and imperative from a prefixed Proto-Slavic *pojьti. * The present te

parole.significato: from (with the source or provenance of or at)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *jьz, from Proto-Indo-European *eǵʰs, *h₁eǵʰs (“from”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *abolnь, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ebol-ni-. First attested in the 16th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)agnę, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʷnós. First attested in the 16th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)azъ, from Proto-Indo-European *éǵh₂. First attested in the 10th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ętro, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁entrom. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *jь appended to Proto-Slavic *ka, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷi-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъto, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos, *kʷid (compare *kʷís). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *kъjь, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷos + relative particle *yos. First attested in the 15th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *kopyto, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱoph₂ós. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *kъrma, *kъrmъ (“food, fodder”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱrh₃-mo-. Original meaning "food" occurs until 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *olbǫdь, from Proto-Indo-European *albʰe(n)d-. First attested in the 16th century.

From Proto-Slavic *olni, from Proto-Indo-European *ol-ney, from *h₂el- (“beyond, other”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian lȃni, Czech loni, vloni, Russian лони́ (loní), and Latin ōlim (“once”). First attested in the 18th century.
From Proto-Slavic *lěpiti, from Proto-Indo-European *leyp- (“to stick”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *lěto (“summer; year”), from Proto-Indo-European *leh₁tom.
From Proto-Slavic *lučь, from Proto-Indo-European *lewk-.
From Proto-Slavic *makъ, from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂kos.
From Proto-Slavic *mati, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr.
From Proto-Slavic *meďa, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos.
From Proto-Slavic *měsęcь, from Proto-Indo-European *mḗh₁n̥s.
From Proto-Slavic *myšь, from Proto-Indo-European *muh₂s.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *modrъ, from Proto-Indo-European *modʰros.
From Proto-Slavic *morvъ, from Proto-Indo-European *morwi-.
From Proto-Slavic *merti, from Proto-Indo-European *mer-.
From Proto-Slavic *mьrtvъ, from Proto-Indo-European *mr̥twós, *mr̥tós, ultimately from the root *mr̥-, *mer- (“to die”).
From Proto-Slavic *nagъ, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *nogʷós (“naked”).
From Proto-Slavic *ne, from Proto-Indo-European *né.
From Proto-Slavic *nogъtь, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nogʰ-.
From Proto-Slavic *o(b), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ebʰi.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *oje, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂oyHsos.
From Proto-Slavic *onъ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énos.
From Proto-Slavic *orěxъ (“nut”), from Proto-Indo-European *areyis-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *otьcь, from Proto-Indo-European *átta.
From Proto-Slavic *paǫkъ, from *pa- + *ǫkъ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enkos (“hook”).
Gerund of plaziti, from Proto-Slavic *pőlziti, from Proto-Indo-European *pelh₂-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *poľe, probably from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, wide”).

parole.significato: fire (occurrence of fire in a certain place or instance, such as an electrical fire or a brush fire)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *požarъ. Equivalent to po- + žár, from Proto-Slavic *žarъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰer(m) (“warm”).
From Proto-Slavic *prijateľь, from Proto-Indo-European *priH- (“dear”).
From Proto-Slavic *pьrstь, originally from Proto-Indo-European *pers- (“rain, dust”).
From Proto-Slavic *orsti, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃er-.

parole.significato: dew (moisture in the air that settles on plants, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *rosà, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁rṓs. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *samъ, from Proto-Indo-European *somHós. First attested in the 10th century.
From Proto-Slavic *sěťi, from Proto-Indo-European *sek- (“to cut”). First attested in the 18th century.
From Proto-Slavic *kora, from Proto-Indo-European *ker-. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *slyšati, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlew-. First attested in the 15th century.
From Proto-Slavic *slùti, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European, from the root *ḱlew- (“to hear”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *snъxa, from Proto-Indo-European *snusós. First attested in the 16th century.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *sъlnьce, from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *stati, from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.
A contraction of earlier stojáti, from Proto-Slavic *stojati, from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.
From Proto-Slavic *strěla, from Proto-Indo-European *strel-, *strēl-, from *ster- (“line, streak, stripe; jet, spurt; beam”).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *strupъ, from Proto-Indo-European *sr(o)up-.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ty, from Proto-Indo-European *túh₂.
From Proto-Slavic *toplъ, from Proto-Indo-European *tep- (“warm”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *uxo, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ous-. First attested in the 16th century.

parole.significato: to know (be certain or sure about (something))
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *věděti, from Proto-Indo-European *wóyde (“to know”). First attested in the 10th century.

parole.significato: branch (woody part of a tree arising from the trunk and usually dividing)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *věja, whence also Old Church Slavonic вѣꙗ (věja, “branch”). Further cognates include Bulgarian вейка (vejka) and ветва (vetva), Russian ветвь (vetvʹ), Slovak vetva. Non-Slavic cognates include Sanskrit वया (vayā́, “branch, twig”) (from Proto-Indo-European *woh₁y-éh₂ (“br
From Proto-Slavic *vędnǫti (through a variant *vęnǫti), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)wendʰ-.
From Proto-Slavic *větrъ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁-. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *věverica (“squirrel”), from Proto-Indo-European *wer-. First attested in the 16th century.

parole.significato: to lead, to guide, to conduct
parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *voditi, from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰ-. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *ǫgъlъ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂engulos (“joint?”), from *h₂eng- (“corner”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *vьlna (“wool”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ (“wool”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *vьrsta, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to rotate, spin”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *sъ(n), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱom.
From Proto-Slavic *zętь, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-.
From Proto-Slavic *zьrělъ, from the verb *zьrěti (“to ripen, to mature”). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂-, which is also the source of zŕno. First attested in the 16th century.
First attested in the 16th century. Inherited from Proto-Slavic *zъvati.

parole.significato: if (supposing that, in the case that)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *či, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷíh₁, initially instrumental singular of pronoun *kʷo-/*kʷe-; compare Latin quī (“how? why?”), Avestan 𐬗𐬌𐬱 (ciš), Old Saxon hwi. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *čelo, from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₃os. First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *čitati, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeyt-. First attested in the 19th century and used as a non-standard synonym of brati.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čьrvь, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷr̥mis (“worm”). First attested in the 16th century.
From Proto-Slavic *šestь, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱs.
From Proto-Slavic *šiti, from Proto-Indo-European *syew-.
From Proto-Slavic *četyre, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres.
From Proto-Slavic *četyre, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwóres.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(š)četъka, *ščetь, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱwek- (“to gape”). See also Sanskrit श्वञ्चते (śvañcate, “to become open”), उच्छ्वङ्क (ucchvaṅka, “cleaving open, gaping”).
From Proto-Slavic *žьlvъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰel-. First attested in the 18th century.
From Proto-Slavic *žeravь, from Proto-Indo-European *gerh₂-. First attested in the 16th century.
